subject: Monitoring GTM sync — telemetry bridge pilot
messages:
From: Alex Foster <alex.foster@grafana.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datadoghq.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@observly.io>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot proposal: telemetry bridge — joint channel + technical pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking a quick call last week. Grafana and Datadog product teams have been talking about a small joint pilot to validate a lightweight telemetry bridge pattern that lets customers route OTLP traffic to both Grafana Cloud and Datadog without double-instrumentation. We think Redwood could be a strong integration partner to provide the runtime + routing piece for customers in our shared SMB/scale segment.

High level ask: would Redwood consider a 6-week technical pilot with one mutual customer (we have an early interest from Observly) to exercise:
- OTLP relay config and auth flows (mTLS / API-key fallback)
- Metric & trace cardinality controls at the edge
- Cost/latency profiling for split ingestion

We can offer co-marketing and a joint case study if the pilot shows clear value.

If this sounds interesting, can we schedule a 30–45m kickoff with your GTM and infra leads this week? I can loop in our engineers to scope the data plane requirements.

Attachment: telemetry-bridge-outline-v0.2.pdf (summary)

Thanks,
Alex Foster
Partnerships, Grafana Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Foster <alex.foster@grafana.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datadoghq.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal: telemetry bridge — joint channel + technical pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear write-up and for looping us in. This aligns with a few of our existing partner goals (low-friction dual-ingest patterns) and I agree a small pilot is the right next step.

Ben and Laura, can you take the lead on the technical scoping? Ben, please collect specific network/auth requirements; Laura, please coordinate pilot success metrics and the MLP for co-sell enablement.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical kick-off (45m) — this week if possible; available windows Tue/Wed 10–12 PST.
2) Redwood team provides a short checklist (networking + auth + sample payloads) for Observly to validate.
3) Draft a one-page MOU describing pilot target, timeline, and shared assets.

Alex — if you can share Observly's point of contact and any non-confidential architecture notes ahead of the kickoff, that will help speed us up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot proposal: telemetry bridge — technical questions before kickoff

Alex / Jordan — quick set of technical questions to validate before the kickoff:

1) Auth model: do you expect customers to use mTLS between edge and Redwood, or use API keys to Redwood with Redwood then using Grafana/Datadog API keys? We can support both but need to validate TLS termination and cert rotation.

2) Traffic shaping: approximate event/metric rates for Observly in peak vs baseline (events/sec, avg payload size). This informs buffer/queue sizing.

3) Retention expectations: are we streaming to both backends synchronously, or buffering and retrying for one (best-effort)?

4) Span/metric cardinality: is there a desire to do pre-aggregation or label filtering at the edge? If so, can you share a short sampling of the schema?

We'll prepare a networking_requirements.xlsx (stubbed) and an integration-checklist.md to share with Observly during the kickoff.

Attachment: networking_requirements.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Foster <alex.foster@grafana.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datadoghq.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@observly.io>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal: telemetry bridge — answers + sample topology

Ben — quick answers inline:

1) Auth model: Observly prefers API-key fronted to a managed relay (Redwood) for now; they will evaluate mTLS later. Grafana and Datadog have service keys that can be exchanged server-to-server, so Redwood would need to support per-destination API keys and a fallback ordering.

2) Traffic shaping: Observly expects baseline ~250 events/sec, peak ~2.5k events/sec; avg payload ~1.6KB.

3) Retention expectations: synchronous fan-out is preferred for the pilot (both destinations must receive the stream), but Retries with a 30s window are acceptable for transient failures.

4) Cardinality: they would like label filtering at the edge (drop some high-card tags) and a small set of pre-aggregations for top-level metrics (60s rollups). We'll attach a sample schema.

Attachment: observly-sample-topology.png (diagram), observly-schema-sample.json

Happy to go through this on the kickoff. Do you want to lock Tuesday 11/23 at 10:30 PST?

—Alex
